name: Transformer Attention - Lecturer A: PyTorch Matrix & Code
voiceSnippet: Let's build the multi-head self-attention module in PyTorch. Look at the forward pass: we project queries, keys, and values using linear layers, reshape with view for num_heads, and compute torch.bmm of Q and K transposed before applying softmax.
documentSnippet: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) V. PyTorch nn.Module forward implementation.

name: Transformer Attention - Lecturer B: Routing Dynamics & Entropy
voiceSnippet: Focus purely on the architectural behavior today; implementation and code syntax are strictly outside today's scope. Consider what happens if the query-key dot products become very large in magnitude: the softmax function gets pushed into regions with infinitesimally small gradients, causing the attention distribution to collapse into a one-hot distribution and halting learning.
documentSnippet: Dot-product scale sensitivity: large values push softmax into vanishing gradient regions.

name: Linux CFS Scheduler - Lecturer A: C Struct & vruntime Math
voiceSnippet: Examine the Linux kernel sched_entity struct on line 42. Notice how vruntime is calculated as delta_exec scaled by the process weight from the sched_prio_to_weight array. Practice tracing the exact vruntime increment in the update_curr function.
documentSnippet: CFS implementation: struct sched_entity, vruntime += delta_exec * (NICE_0_LOAD / se->load.weight).

name: Linux CFS Scheduler - Lecturer B: Fairness Intuition & Trade-offs
voiceSnippet: Leave low-level C structs and kernel code for the lab section; here we only reason about scheduling fairness. Think about what happens when an I/O-bound process sleeps for a long time and then wakes up: if it retained its old vruntime, it would monopolize the CPU and starve interactive tasks. Explore why CFS must clamp sleeping tasks to the minimum vruntime of the runqueue.
documentSnippet: Completely Fair Scheduling principles: proportional fairness, latency sensitivity, sleeper fairness trade-off.
acceptableHardReasoningProperties: Predicts system starvation anomaly if waking sleeper processes retained stale runtime
Evaluates fairness vs latency trade-off when clamping vruntime for waking tasks

name: Conceptual-Hard: Mutation Testing Fault Detection Dynamics
voiceSnippet: Why does a test suite with 100% line and branch coverage frequently fail to catch critical production defects? Investigate the difference between executing a statement and verifying its outcome. In mutation testing, we inject artificial faults into the program; if your tests still pass, your tests executed the code without asserting correctness.
documentSnippet: Software Testing Metrics: Statement coverage, branch coverage, mutation score, equivalent mutants.
acceptableHardReasoningProperties: Explains the difference between code reachability and assertion effectiveness (Oracle problem)

name: Conceptual-Hard: Byzantine Fault Tolerance Node Quorum Dynamics
voiceSnippet: Why do crash fault tolerant systems like Raft only require 2f+1 nodes to survive f failures, while Byzantine fault tolerant systems strictly require 3f+1 nodes? Think through what breaks: a crashed node simply goes silent, but a Byzantine traitor can tell half the cluster yes and the other half no, actively constructing conflicting majorities.
documentSnippet: Byzantine Agreement: Oral messages algorithm, Lamport-Shostak-Pease bound N >= 3f + 1.
acceptableHardReasoningProperties: Evaluates why equivocation (two-faced messaging) requires overlapping quorums of 2f+1 honest nodes

name: True Deficit: Version Control Systems Taxonomy
voiceSnippet: Version control systems allow software teams to track changes over time. Centralized systems like Subversion and CVS store all project history on a single central server. Distributed systems like Git and Mercurial give every developer a full copy of the repository history.
documentSnippet: VCS Classification: Centralized VCS vs Distributed VCS.

name: True Deficit: Web Architecture Tier Overview
voiceSnippet: In standard multi-tier web applications, the client tier runs in the user's web browser, the application tier runs the business logic on a backend server, and the database tier persists data to disk.
documentSnippet: Three-Tier Architecture: Presentation Tier, Application Tier, Data Tier.
